note: An (the sky) and Ki (the earth) are the first pair (the 'parents' of the world).
explanation: An and Ki are the 'parents' of the world in Sumerian cosmology [S5].

note: An (with Ki) is the parent of Enlil.
An (with Ki) is the parent of Enki (in some accounts).
Ki (with An) is the parent of Enlil.
Apsu (the fresh water) and Tiamat (the salt water) are the two primeval waters (a 'pair').
explanation: Apsu and Tiamat are the two primeval waters in Sumerian cosmology [S3][S5].

note: Enki slays Apsu (in the Atrahasis) — the creation-of-humanity story.
explanation: Enki slays Apsu because his noise disturbs his rest; humanity is made from Apsu's flesh [S3].

note: Enki allies with the gods against Apsu (in the Atrahasis).
Enki (Ea) is the father of Marduk (in the Enuma Elish).
Tiamat and Kingu are a 'pair' (Kingu is her general and consort).
Marduk slays Tiamat (in the Enuma Elish).
explanation: Marduk slays Tiamat with his bow, net, and 'rakasu' winds [S1].

note: Marduk splits Tiamat's body in two to make the sky (upper half) and the earth (lower half).
Marduk slays Kingu (in the Enuma Elish).
Marduk takes the 'Tablet of Destinies' from Kingu (the symbol of cosmic authority).
Enlil and Enki are siblings (both sons of An and Ki, in some accounts).
Enlil and Ninlil are a 'pair'.
Enlil (with Ninlil) is the parent of Nanna (the moon god).
Ninlil (with Enlil) is the parent of Nanna.
(Mythic) In one text, Enlil seduces Ninlil (in the underworld) and she bears Nanna there.
Nanna (with Ningal) is the parent of Utu (the sun god).
Nanna (with Ningal) is the parent of Inanna (the love/war goddess).
Ningal (with Nanna) is the parent of Utu.
Ningal (with Nanna) is the parent of Inanna.
Utu and Inanna are siblings (both children of Nanna).
Nanna and Ningal are a 'pair'.
Enki is the father of Nabu (the god of writing).
Inanna and Ereshkigal are sisters (in some accounts).
explanation: In some accounts they are sisters; in others they are adversaries [S4][S5].

note: Inanna descends to the underworld (to Ereshkigal's funeral) and is killed there.
Ereshkigal and Nergal are a 'pair' (the 'Nergal and Ereshkigal' marriage myth).
(Mythic) In the 'Nergal and Ereshkigal' myth, Nergal 'rapes' (or marries) Ereshkigal.
Nergal (as Ereshkigal's consort) is her 'pair'.
An and Antu (Anatum) are a 'pair'.
The Tablets of Destiny are the emblem of the highest divine authority.
Marduk takes the Tablets when he is set over the gods.
Nabu, god of writing, is associated with the tablets of fate.
